- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–2% for 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.8, -0.4, +0.6), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 periods to anchor forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise.
